column1: # `docs/standards/chunk-format.md` declares this vocabulary in prose and says "Separate phrases with
# a comma", so a cell is a **set of tokens** and enforcement belongs on the token. Measured over
# `chunks/`: 56 distinct cells but **46 distinct tokens**, 9 of them the declared ones.
# One row per token. `status` is one of:
#   declared  - a vocabulary member. The 9 from the specification page, plus the methods the corpus
#               carries that the page never named; those are admitted under the spelling they
#               already have rather than renamed to something no submitter wrote.
#   alias     - a case, separator or spelling variant of a declared token. `canonical` names it.
#   pending   - present in the corpus and not decided. A curator's call, listed with the question.
# **Not a gate.** `vdjdb qc` reports an unknown or `pending` token as an advisory finding and never
# fails, the same treatment every other table in `proofreading/` gets. A submission naming a method
# nobody has seen is a method nobody has seen, not a defect.
# Four aliases move a confidence score, because `score/confidence.py` matches **substrings** of the
# lowercased cell and a typo misses the substring it was meant to hit:
# `antigen-loaded-targed` and `antigen-expressing cells` (61) do not contain `targets`. Correcting
# the spelling gives those 123 records the score their method earns. Every other alias here already
# matched, so it cannot move a score.
